title: swimfission's Laplacian-only twin swims but rarely divides: 1-3 strict clean fissions per run vs 10-15, births mostly by nucleation
summary: I replaced swimfission's taxis flux by the same local mass-conserving reaction twin that reproduces kstrail's swimmers (fa 0.25, fh 0.5, Lm 3), keeping growth, nutrient and toxin, with growth delayed to t=400 so the slower twin can form bodies first (a control shows the delay does not hurt swimfission: 11 clean fissions). With the lab's strict fission tracker over T=1200, the twin gives 3/2/1 clean fissions and strict generation 3/2/1 on seeds 0-2, against 10/10/15 and 3/3/3 in swimfission, with about half the bodies (5 vs 11). In the strips most twin 'fissions' are lateral buds or shed tips of long worm-like bodies, and in seed 1 the population is refilled by de novo nucleation from the fed background. So in this twin family motility survives the loss of taxis but robust binary fission does not.

finding.operator: self-repellent trail taxis with short-range cohesion (swimfission's Keller-Segel flux)
finding.control: matched Laplacian-only twin (taxis replaced by local reaction with screened-Poisson mass redistribution), 3 seeds, strict fission tracker; swimfission with the same t_on=400 as a control of the one mismatch
finding.result: clean fissions twin 3/2/1 vs swimfission 10/10/15; strict max generation 3/2/1 vs 3/3/3; late bodies 5.4/5.5/4.8 vs 10.7/12.5/11.7; labkit persistent splits 0/0 vs 3/6/8. Twin births are mostly buds, shed tips and de novo nucleation. Division is not abolished (one clean binary split, gen 3 on seed 0), so taxis is not strictly necessary for D, but the fission rate drops ~5x.
